doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Names of parents, grandparents and relatives
summary: Freeman gives his parents', brothers' and grandparents' names, the origins of LaVon and 'Vonski', and his mother's eight siblings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Next thing you know. So what were . . . ? Let me get some of these people’s names – complete names – on record. I guess we start with your parents’ names.

My father’s name was George Thomas Freeman, Sr. My mother’s name was Earle – E-a-r-l-e – but I was named after her – Karee – that’s K-a-r-double-e. Grandberry was her maiden name. Of course she married my father, Freeman. Bruz’s name is Eldridge Edmond Freeman.
That’s your older brother.
Yeah. My name is Earl LaVon. But it’s not L-a-v-o-n. It’s L-a-capital V-o-n. capital L-a, capital V-o-n Freeman.
Where did they get the LaVon from?
That was my father’s best friend. His name was LaVon. Because I asked himself, to how – where he get that goofy name from? He told me to hush. Then, George, he’s a junior, George Thomas Freeman, Jr.
You know your grandparents’ names?
My grandfather’s name was – the best I can do with him is William Grandberry.
On your mother’s side.
Yeah. His mother’s name was – I didn’t know her maiden name. What was her first name? I should know that. She was almost a full-blooded Indian.
I always thought you had Native American in you.
Really?
Yeah, I could kind of see that.

It might have come from her. What was her name? Boy, she – she’d slap me for not – oh, Janey – Jane. Jane, I’ll say, Grandberry, because I can’t remember her maiden name. They had eight children. My mother was the second. She was the second daughter. The one I was named after, that Vonski stuff comes from my mother’s youngest sister. Her name was Teneski.
Oh, that’s where you got all that “ski”?
She’s the only one still living. Boy, if I told you their names, because the boy’s names – dig these names. The elder boy’s name was Picolla. Then the next one was Blanco.
It sounds like cartoons.
Yeah. Wait a minute. The third one’s name was Saverra, and the fourth one’s name was Farazil.
Fanzil?

Farazil. Now, the girl’s names were a little bit better. My mother’s eldest sister – because she was the second girl – her name was Viva. My mother’s name was Earle. The next daughter’s name was – oh man, it’s – Baymeta.
She has an imagination.

And the last one, the one who’s living, her name’s Teneski. I used to be just in love with her, puppy love. I used to just follow her around, pull on her apron strings. They used to call me Little Ski. So that’s where all that come from, from years and years and years and years back.
And your father’s? Do you know your father’s mother and father?
Oh yeah. Let’s see now. You know, it’s funny. Her name was Lila Freeman, and his name was Dave Freeman.
Her maiden name was Freeman?
No. I never knew her maiden name.
I can’t remember my grandmother’s maiden name.
I knew it, but I just – I’d have to look it up or something. And then Calvin Freeman. That was my father’s brother. His sister’s name was Margaret Kendell.

I’m not going to go real far into that, because I don’t think we’re doing genealogy here. Just want the grandparents. You told me a little bit about the kind of music that they listened to in your house, at home.
